movement_source: row 'Loan impairment expense/(benefit)', column 30 Jun 25 -> column 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's loan impairment expense (LIE, continuing operations, cash basis) rose $62 million or 9% to $788 million in FY26 from $726 million in FY25. The loss rate rose 1 basis point to 8 basis points of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA +7% to $1,087,560m). The bank's own provision-type bridge (Appendix 2.2) sums exactly to the $62m: net collective provision funding +$150m ($606m vs $456m); net new and increased individual provisioning −$17m ($422m vs $439m); write-back of individually assessed provisions −$71m ($240m vs $169m). Where it arose: Retail Banking Services +$106m to $378m; New Zealand +$11m to $66m; Corporate Centre +$6m ($1m vs $5m benefit); partly offset by Business Banking −$45m to $310m and Institutional Banking & Markets −$16m to $33m. The results presentation corroborates ($788m, +8.5% vs FY25; divisional bullets +$106m/−$45m/−$16m/+$18m NZD). The FY25 book corroborates the FY25 endpoint ($726m; collective funding $456m). Half-on-half context: 2H26 $469m vs 1H26 $319m (+47%).

drivers.narrative: Bank's stated reasons: portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty. Where: RBS +$106m to $378m (cost-of-living pressures; home 90+ arrears 0.69%→0.75%); NZ +$11m to $66m (deteriorating unemployment outlook); Corporate Centre +$6m ($1m vs $(5)m benefit); BB and IB&M collective increases partly offset their falls. Volume vs risk-migration split not disclosed.

drivers.bank_label: Net new and increased individual provisioning
drivers.narrative: New and increased individually assessed charges fell to $422m from $439m. Where: BB −$45m to $310m on lower individually assessed provision charges; IB&M −$16m to $33m on release of individually assessed provisions; NZ also cites lower individually assessed provisions. The bank gives no group-level reason beyond the divisional drivers.

Write-backs of individually assessed provisions rose to $240m from $169m, cutting the charge. BB cites 'an increase in write-backs'; IB&M released single-name provisions. Context: collective recoveries rose to $160m from $130m; collective write-offs rose to $618m from $512m, absorbed in the net collective row.

drivers.bank_label: Collective provisions: risk migration (not separately quantified)
drivers.narrative: Not separately quantified: the bank prints collective provisions as one net row. Migration reasons named: increased geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty (RBS, BB, IB&M), deteriorating NZ unemployment outlook, rising cost-of-living pressures and arrears (home 90+ 0.69%→0.75%; consumer finance 1.03%→1.18%).

notable_items: None within LIE. The presentation's separate 'Restructuring and notable items' line ($170m FY26) covers NZ legal-proceedings provisions, an ASIC Better Banking goodwill payment and customer remediation — not loan impairment.

disagreements.explanation: The FY26 book restates comparatives to continuing-operations presentation; the group total is unchanged at $726m. The restated comparatives are preferred for the where-layer.

disagreements.topic: New Zealand divisional LIE movement FY26 vs FY25
disagreements.explanation: The presentation quotes the NZ division in NZD; the results book quotes it in AUD. Same movement, different currency.

disagreements.topic: LIE growth rate FY26 vs FY25
disagreements.explanation: 8.5% rounds to 9%; both documents print the same levels ($788m vs $726m).

limitations: No FY26-vs-FY25 waterfall chart is published for LIE; the quantified bridge is built from the bank's provision-type table (Appendix 2.2). Component movements are my subtraction of the two printed period columns; the bank states only the total (+$62m, 9%).
Collective provisions are printed as one net row; the split between portfolio growth (volume) and risk migration is not quantified — the bank gives narrative reasons only.
Write-offs ($618m vs $512m collective; $242m vs $229m individual) and recoveries ($160m vs $130m) are absorbed inside the net rows; gross effects are context, not separate bridge bars.
Provision balance movements (collective closing $5,685m vs $5,561m; individually assessed $791m vs $816m) are stock context, not part of the charge bridge.
Non-retail overlays fell from $0.5bn (Jun 25) to $nil (Jun 26) per the RWA footnote; the LIE bridge does not isolate overlay effects.
Divisional comparatives restated to continuing operations; the FY25 book's original split differs slightly (RBS 274/BB 353 vs restated 272/355).
NZ divisional movement is +$11m AUD in the results book; the presentation quotes +$18m NZD.
